messages:
maria: heads-up — after the CUDA driver bump on prod-canary (535.80) we see a consistent p95 latency regression for mid-length requests (seq 128-512) on H100 pools, ~18-22% increase. filing here before we spam infra.
raj: ack, can you paste the perf numbers and which model/variant?
maria: model: rdx-large-v1 (fp16 q4_0), variant: default. baseline (pre-bump) p95=120ms, post-bump p95=145ms on same workload. throughput slightly down under sustained QPS.
lee: quick profiler snapshot (canary host h100-can-12):
```
# runtime-kvprof --pid 2345 --interval 10s
Kernel picks by seq range:
  seq<=64 -> fast_fused_attn (vectorized)
  65-512 -> aten_attn_v2 (fallback slow path)
  >512 -> block_fused_attn (same as before)
KV-cache hit ratio unchanged (~98%)
Batching skew increased for mid-seq (avg batch size -1.2)
```
lee: note: before driver bump autotune had settled on fast_fused_attn for the 65-512 band, but now the heuristic picks aten_attn_v2. kernel timings per-token show aten_attn_v2 ~1.4x slower for these seqs.
olivia: do we know if autotuner re-ran after driver upgrade? maybe nvcc/kernel differences changed perf ranking.
maria: autotuner did a background probe loop during deploy; logs show re-eval for the model on 2026-01-31 03:12UTC and it picked aten_attn_v2 for that seq band.
raj: can we force a kernel override? risk is correctness/regressions but for rollback it's fine.
lee: runtime exposes KERNEL_FORCE env var per model in config: `KERNEL_FORCE=fast_fused_attn` — that'll override picker. also there's AUTOTUNE_ENABLE=false to disable probes.
olivia: plan suggestion:
  1) emergency canary rollback: set KERNEL_FORCE=fast_fused_attn on canary model instances (non-disruptive) and measure for 30m
  2) if stable -> propagate to dedicated pools and trigger staged rollout
  3) revert driver bump on the small-scale region (if kernel override insufficient)
  4) update autotune scoring to prefer throughput over single-batch latency for seq 65-512, and add gating so kernel choice doesn't flip on microbench jitter
raj: +1. Also add a gate so autotune requires >3 independent runs across different kernel builds before making a persistent pick.
sre-bot: canary pool hosts: 12 healthy, 2 in draining. I can set environment on the 10 active nodes if you want.
deploy-bot: rollback runbook: https://go/release/runbooks/kernel-rollback (runs set-env across pool + healthcheck)
maria: I'll kick the override now on canary and watch. posting quick check script:
```
# check p95 for rdx-large-v1
python infra/bench/check_p95.py --model rdx-large-v1 --window 600
```
maria: override applied to canary at 2012345702, measuring...
lee: after 12m snapshot: p95 down to 123ms (near baseline), throughput recovered. batch size distribution returned to pre-bump.
olivia: good sign. action items:
  - mara/lee: open autotune bug, attach profiler traces and kernel timings
  - infra: add a metric to console: kernel-choice-per-seqlen + confidence score
  - product: alert teams using rdx-large-v1 about transient perf noise
raj: for longer term: add a small synthetic probe in the deployment pipeline that runs kernels under the exact driver+lib versions we plan to roll, compare ranking, and block if core picks flip for >10% perf change.
maria: noted. I'll file the incident and attach logs. thumbs up if we can promote the override out of canary after 1h of stability.
lee: +1 :thumbsup:
olivia: +1
sre-bot: scheduled health-check job every 5m for the overridden pool for the next 6h.
maria: closing loop here — will post the incident ticket once created (inc/2026-00124)."
